# Report card {#sec-reportcard}

```{python}
exec(open("_common.py").read())
import json
card = json.loads((ROOT / "models" / "scorecard.json").read_text())
w, s, t, tt = card["winner"], card["spread"], card["total"], card["team_total"]
```

This chapter answers the simplest question: **how often is the model right, for each
thing it predicts, compared with the sportsbooks?** Every number comes from seasons the
model never saw. Each season from 2021 to 2025 is predicted by a model trained only on
earlier seasons (`scripts/scorecard.py`, read live from `models/scorecard.json`).

## The scorecard

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scorecard
#| tbl-cap: "Out-of-sample report card, 2021–2025. Market = closing lines (moneylines de-vigged; swapped moneylines removed)."
pct = lambda x: f"{100 * x:.1f}%"
pts = lambda x: f"{x:.2f} pts"
rows = [
    ("Winner", "Picks the right winner", pct(w["model"]["accuracy"]), pct(w["market"]["accuracy"])),
    ("Winner", "AUC (0.5 coin flip, 1 perfect)", f"{w['model']['auc']:.3f}", f"{w['market']['auc']:.3f}"),
    ("Winner", "Brier score (lower is better)", f"{w['model']['brier']:.3f}", f"{w['market']['brier']:.3f}"),
    ("Spread", "Average miss on the final margin", pts(s["mae_margin_model"]), pts(s["mae_margin_market"])),
    ("Spread", "Covers, model's side vs opening line", pct(s["ats_vs_open"]["win_rate"]), "—"),
    ("Spread", "Covers, model's side vs closing line", pct(s["ats_vs_close"]["win_rate"]), "—"),
    ("Total", "Average miss on total points", pts(t["mae_model"]), pts(t["mae_market"])),
    ("Total", "Wins, model's side vs opening line", pct(t["ou_vs_open"]["win_rate"]), "—"),
    ("Total", "Wins, model's side vs closing line", pct(t["ou_vs_close"]["win_rate"]), "—"),
    ("Team points", "Average miss on each team's points", pts(tt["mae_model"]), pts(tt["mae_market"])),
]
pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["Target", "Measure", "Model", "Sportsbooks"]).set_index("Target")
```

Reading it:

- **Picking winners: good.** The model picks the right winner about 7 times in 10, close
  to the sportsbooks. An AUC around 0.77 is solid for college football.
- **Beating the price: not yet.** Against the spread and the total, betting the model's
  side lands near 50%, and you need 52.4% at −110 just to break even. Betting the
  moneyline where the model is more confident than the books returned **−4.5%**
  (@sec-decisions).
- **Accuracy gap:** the books are about 0.4–0.6 points more accurate on margins and
  totals.

## Halves and quarters

```{python}
#| label: tbl-periods-card
#| tbl-cap: "Halves and quarters: average miss vs guessing the average (no sportsbook lines yet)."
per = pd.DataFrame(card["periods"]).T
per["improvement"] = (100 * (per.mae_model / per.mae_constant - 1)).map(lambda x: f"{x:.0f}%")
per.rename(columns={"mae_model": "model (pts)", "mae_constant": "guess the average (pts)"}).round(2)
```

## Where the model falls behind

The most useful part of a report card is where the grade is lowest. The gap is how many
points worse than the sportsbooks the model's margin is.

```{python}
#| label: fig-gaps
#| fig-cap: "Margin error gap vs the closing line, by part of the season and by spread size (points; lower is better)."
seg_w = pd.DataFrame(card["segments"]["week_bucket"]).T
seg_s = pd.DataFrame(card["segments"]["spread_bucket"]).T
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6.5, 2.8))
for ax, seg, title in ((axes[0], seg_w, "Part of season"), (axes[1], seg_s, "Spread size")):
    ax.barh(range(len(seg)), seg.gap, color=ORANGE, height=0.6)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(seg))); ax.set_yticklabels(seg.index, fontsize=8)
    ax.invert_yaxis(); ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
    for i, v in enumerate(seg.gap):
        ax.text(v + 0.03, i, f"+{v:.1f}", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(seg_w.gap.max(), seg_s.gap.max()) * 1.25); bar_ends(ax)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Three weak spots stand out: **the first weeks of the season**, **bowls and the
playoff**, and **blowouts** (spreads above three touchdowns). In the middle and late
regular season the model is almost level with the market. The first weak spot was
addressed with preseason information (@sec-improvements); the others are on the roadmap.
